Bounds, types and counts over the buffers

Source: R/kernel.R
geo_box.Rd

geo_box() gives each geometry's bounding box and geo_box_all() the one box around them all, both as a geo_extent(), computed over the coordinate buffers with no R object per geometry (design section 6.7). Z and M ranges come when the geometries have them. A null geometry's box is NA and an empty one's NaN.

Usage

geo_box(x, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_box_all(x, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_types(x)

geo_dims(x)

geo_n_coords(x)

Arguments

x

A geo_vctr.

lossy

As for geo_as_wkb(): "error", "warn" or "allow" a planar box for non-planar edges.

Value

geo_box() and geo_box_all(): a geo_extent. geo_types(), geo_dims(): character vectors. geo_n_coords(): an integer vector.

Details

Bounds are planar. For a non-planar edge type a planar box can miss an edge that bulges past its vertices or crosses the antimeridian, so on geometries with edges geo_box() is a zugeo_edges_error unless lossy says otherwise.

geo_types(), geo_dims() and geo_n_coords() give each geometry's type, dimensions and number of coordinates (NA for a null).

Examples

x <- geo_vctr(c("POINT (1 2)", "LINESTRING Z (0 0 1, 3 4 5)", NA))
geo_box(x)
#> <geo_extent[3]; crs none; edges planar>
#> [1] [1 2 NaN, 1 2 NaN]
#> [2] [0 0 1, 3 4 5]
#> [3] <null>
geo_box_all(x)
#> <geo_extent[1]; crs none; edges planar>
#> [1] [0 0 1, 3 4 5]
geo_types(x)
#> [1] "point"      "linestring" NA          
geo_n_coords(x)
#> [1]  1  2 NA
